sources.title: AI That Works #42 No Vibes Allowed (transcript)
sources.note: Live RPI session using Riptide (new CodeLayer) on a BAML WASM task; rich in Dex workflow rationale.

sources.title: AI That Works #40 Applying 12-Factor Principles to Coding Agent SDKs (README and meta only)
sources.note: No transcript supplied; only episode description and topic list.

cards.source_title: AI That Works #42 No Vibes Allowed
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: we've done a lot of replacing the usage of prompting for control flow.
cards.claim: The rebuilt workflow splits a monolithic prompt into separate steps so ordinary control flow, not prompt wording, enforces the sequence.
cards.evidence_detail: Describes the Riptide rebuild moving from 'magic words' appended to prompts to a 4-5 step workflow; no numbers.
cards.landing: Phase routine in ship plan section 0: encode skipped-prone steps as separate skills or scripted workflow stages rather than prose in CLAUDE.md
cards.inventory_ref: AI That Works #40 entry (2026-01-19): 'Also #39 Latency; #41 Email is All You Need; #42 No Vibes Allowed' (mention only)

cards.source_title: AI That Works #42 No Vibes Allowed
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: we've taken a long prompt with 50 instructions and split it up into three smaller prompts
cards.claim: The old combined planning prompt had steps that got skipped, so it was split into three prompts (design discussion, structure outline, plan), each with fewer instructions.
cards.evidence_detail: Dex says steps 'could get skipped often' in the single prompt; the fix is stated as working but not measured.
cards.landing: Phase routine and CLAUDE.md trim: long multi-step instructions become several small skills invoked per step

cards.source_title: AI That Works #42 No Vibes Allowed
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: the goal of research is really to like compress truth, to compress the state of the world today
cards.claim: Research should be objective and carry no knowledge of what is being built, so the model does not bake in implementation opinions.
cards.evidence_detail: Explained as the reason research is kept separate from the ticket; observed failure is the model focusing on solving the ticket.
cards.landing: P1 cold-resume trial and any explorer/diagnosis step: recover facts from the repo without the task framing; fixflow-explorer agent prompt

cards.source_title: AI That Works #42 No Vibes Allowed
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: generate not a research document, but a set of objective questions.
cards.claim: A lightweight pass turns the ticket into a list of objective research questions that the human can edit, and a fresh context window answers them without seeing the ticket.
cards.evidence_detail: Trialled 'a lot' with 'really good results'; replaces the skilled-user habit of hand-writing neutral questions.
cards.landing: Workflow script: questions stage then fresh-context researcher; could feed the knowledge-store diagnosis step

cards.source_title: AI That Works #42 No Vibes Allowed
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: you don't want it to read the file because you don't want the input query.
cards.claim: The researcher context must be stripped of the original ticket text, because knowing what is being built biases research.
cards.evidence_detail: Said when Vaibhav wanted to keep the input query; Vaibhav notes he found it sometimes useful, so there is disagreement.
cards.landing: Fresh-context refuter and explorer briefs: pass questions, not the proposed answer

cards.source_title: AI That Works #42 No Vibes Allowed
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: I actually no longer recommend that people read those.
cards.claim: He no longer recommends reading 1000-2000 line implementation plans, because that duplicates code review; the shorter design discussion and structure outline are what humans should review.
cards.evidence_detail: Observed users doing 'double code review' on plan and then on the PR; plans are 80-90% right with late tweaks. Vaibhav disagrees and reads plans, finding bugs.
cards.landing: Ship plan section 0 owner view / decisions journal: keep the human-read artifact short and high-level

cards.source_title: AI That Works #42 No Vibes Allowed
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Don't make humans read any more markdown than they have to
cards.claim: Design docs are for team mental alignment and human leverage; share the design discussion around rather than the plan.
cards.evidence_detail: Stated principle, tied to avoiding 'pan the aster review' pull requests.
cards.landing: One-page owner view; docs shared between sessions

cards.source_title: AI That Works #42 No Vibes Allowed
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: you can't actually test anything until it's done.
cards.claim: Agents default to horizontal plans (API, then DB, then services, then UI); order steps as vertical slices with a unit or integration check between them so the model can verify as it goes.
cards.evidence_detail: Reasoned from experience: failing at the end of 2000 lines costs more context; analogy to writing 50 lines then running a test.
cards.landing: Phase definition in ship plan: each phase ends with a check; fail-before/pass-after per register id

cards.source_title: AI That Works #42 No Vibes Allowed
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: The phase should not be so big that the model can't complete it in one context window.
cards.claim: Size phases so each fits one context window yet leaves something to verify at the end; merge phases when the split is artificial.
cards.evidence_detail: Heuristic with a stated sweet spot that depends on codebase, taste and testability; no numbers.
cards.landing: Ship plan phase sizing under 'one phase per new session'

cards.source_title: AI That Works #42 No Vibes Allowed
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: every document you create becomes part of your accumulated context window
cards.claim: Each stage's document is carried forward as context so the final plan can be executed with one context window per phase.
cards.evidence_detail: Narrated while showing reference documents attached to the structure-outline session.
cards.landing: Phase routine: documents as hand-off between fresh sessions

cards.source_title: AI That Works #42 No Vibes Allowed
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: I don't believe in compaction.
cards.claim: He avoids compaction; he will auto-compact when casually riffing but treats it as important when dialed in on a thousand-line change.
cards.evidence_detail: Brief statements; contrasted with Vaibhav, who uses auto-compact routinely.
cards.landing: Context budget defence: one phase per new session rather than compacting

cards.source_title: AI That Works #42 No Vibes Allowed
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: fork out into what I call like proof mode or like learning test mode
cards.claim: During design, fork out to write tiny proofs of concept that demonstrate a claimed behaviour, because every model confidently states how something works and misses key details.
cards.evidence_detail: Described as something he does sometimes; no numbers.
cards.landing: Refuter/verifier step: require a runnable repro rather than a model assertion; knowledge-store 'verified diagnoses'

cards.source_title: AI That Works #42 No Vibes Allowed
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: just because it said I found nothing of this on the web doesn't mean it hasn't happened.
cards.claim: The Claude web-search researcher subagent is weaker than ChatGPT deep research, so 'found nothing' is a signal, not proof.
cards.evidence_detail: Aside after the agent reported zero production examples of an approach.
cards.landing: Verifier guidance: treat absence reports from search subagents as weak evidence

cards.source_title: AI That Works #42 No Vibes Allowed
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: it's easier to catch it now than halfway through implementation.
cards.claim: Review the design/outline closely because an architectural wrong assumption in an early artifact flows unseen into the code; catching it early is cheaper.
cards.evidence_detail: Live example: playground crate about to depend on the wrong crate, which an import-boundary tool would later catch.
cards.landing: Ship plan review points before implementation; import-linter contracts as the later backstop

cards.source_title: AI That Works #42 No Vibes Allowed
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: you're not doing the thinking, which is like what the engineers are being paid for.
cards.claim: Accepting every model choice without reading the options means the human has not done the engineering, and a reviewer then has to review everything.
cards.evidence_detail: Response to Vaibhav's remark on juniors pressing enter repeatedly.
cards.landing: Owner/reviewer step in phase routine: require evidence of human decisions in the decisions journal

cards.source_title: AI That Works #42 No Vibes Allowed
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: safety through culture rather than through systems that enforce stuff.
cards.claim: At his first job there was no enforced review rule, no admin override gate and no pre-push or pre-commit hooks; discipline came from culture, and it worked at about 20 engineers.
cards.evidence_detail: Personal recollection; offered as a counterweight when Vaibhav proposed an enforced review gate.
cards.landing: Hooks / pre-commit gate decision (skipped by harness review): reopens the question; marks as a hooks-related idea

cards.source_title: AI That Works #42 No Vibes Allowed
cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: requires human review for the check to pass if there's like more than a thousand lines
cards.claim: A CI gate that requires explicit human sign-off when change magnitude (or an LLM-judged complexity) passes a threshold, instead of per-file owners.
cards.evidence_detail: Vaibhav's proposal (with CodSpeed performance-regression approval as precedent); Dex restates it and asks if GitHub already offers it.
cards.landing: CI fourth check or reviewer rule: size-triggered human approval for risky phases

cards.source_title: AI That Works #42 No Vibes Allowed
cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Human wall clock time.
cards.claim: Optimise for human wall-clock time, not token cost: start the next stage before finishing review of the previous one and discard it if the earlier output was wrong.
cards.evidence_detail: Vaibhav's practice ('screw tokens', pipelining); Dex agrees and notes outlines are fast to produce.
cards.landing: Effort/cost routing policy (L1): pipelined stages trade tokens for latency

cards.source_title: AI That Works #42 No Vibes Allowed
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: It's not that hard to just rewind, take your research and be like, cool, go do a follow-up
cards.claim: If a research gap shows up late, rewind to the research document, run a follow-up research and resume from there, so skipping a detailed review of research is low risk.
cards.evidence_detail: Said in explaining why he sometimes skips reviewing questions and research on smaller tasks.
cards.landing: Phase routine rework path: resume from a saved artifact rather than restart

cards.source_title: AI That Works #42 No Vibes Allowed
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: the ceiling goes up with how much of this context engineering and design
cards.claim: Task complexity that can be solved rises with the amount of up-front context engineering; trivial edits need none, mid-size tasks need plan-and-implement, large cross-module work needs the full flow.
cards.evidence_detail: Answer to a question on plan-then-implement versus full RPI; Vaibhav says plan-to-implement only works for simple tasks.
cards.landing: Phase routine tiering: lighter routine for small phases, full routine for large ones

cards.source_title: AI That Works #42 No Vibes Allowed
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: plan for phases one and two because they're actually huge.
cards.claim: For very large work, write several research files and a structure outline of about 10 phases, then carve plans for subsets of phases that are each independently shippable; a 20,000-line PR was shipped in two parts this way.
cards.evidence_detail: Kyle's 20k-line PR used three structure outlines and 3-4 plans; plans of 10k lines would eat too much context just to read.
cards.landing: Ship plan decomposition of the 40 phases; plan-per-phase-group

cards.source_title: AI That Works #42 No Vibes Allowed
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: give the model four options to ask questions about the problem
cards.claim: Every stage can surface open questions and the human can re-steer at each stage; research open questions are answered in design, design questions in the outline.
cards.evidence_detail: Explains the structure of the enhanced RPI flow; goal is to be thoughtful about edge cases before implementation.
cards.landing: Phase routine: explicit open-questions section carried between stages

cards.source_title: AI That Works #42 No Vibes Allowed
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: it might resort to like weird said shit and stuff.
cards.claim: Two agents editing the same markdown file trigger 'file modified' errors and the agent can crash out into odd edit approaches, so avoid parallel writes to one file.
cards.evidence_detail: Observed live; suggests a CRDT-style file layer as a fix; Vaibhav says it is why he avoids parallel writes.
cards.landing: Workflow script rule: one writer per artifact file; evidence folders per agent

cards.source_title: AI That Works #42 No Vibes Allowed
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: an autonomy slider, where it's like, once you approve the structure outline
cards.claim: Plans an autonomy setting where approving the structure outline lets the system write the plan, create a worktree and implementer, and run until a PR is ready.
cards.evidence_detail: Product roadmap statement for Riptide; Vaibhav already lets the implementer run in a loop after the outline.
cards.landing: Workflow tool: single approval gate before unattended implementation

cards.source_title: AI That Works #42 No Vibes Allowed
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: We're very careful with like modifying people's system prompts or injecting context that they can't see
cards.claim: The tool deliberately does not inject hidden context (such as the current task) into the system prompt; the skill needs the task named explicitly.
cards.evidence_detail: Explains why the 'iterate design discussion' skill did not know which task Vaibhav was on.
cards.landing: Skills design: pass the task/phase identifier explicitly as a skill argument

cards.source_title: AI That Works #42 No Vibes Allowed
cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: Tickets usually start anywhere from 2 to 70 lines.
cards.claim: Measured artifact sizes across 12 tasks: tickets 2-70 lines, research 400-1000, design questions about half that, plans around 1000 up to 3000.
cards.evidence_detail: Vaibhav counted lines in his task folder on screen; Dex confirms plans end up around a thousand lines; single sample.
cards.landing: Benchmark for sizing phase documents against context budget

cards.source_title: AI That Works #42 No Vibes Allowed
cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: I hate the fact that we don't keep all the options around.
cards.claim: Design documents should keep short descriptions of rejected options so later steps and reviewers know a decision was made deliberately.
cards.evidence_detail: Vaibhav's request; Dex says it is queued as a product fix.
cards.landing: Decisions journal in the draft PR body: record rejected alternatives

cards.source_title: AI That Works #42 No Vibes Allowed
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: you would be surprised how much of the context window gets used
cards.claim: A fresh context spends much of its window finding where things are; research that returns file and line references saves downstream context.
cards.evidence_detail: Dex observation; Vaibhav says code references make grepping easier in later stages.
cards.landing: Explorer agent output format (file:line map) and knowledge-store entries

cards.source_title: AI That Works #42 No Vibes Allowed
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: you don't really want to be feeding SVG paths straight to an LLM
cards.claim: Challenges a generated architecture diagram being fed as SVG; prefers an intermediate text representation that is LLM friendly.
cards.evidence_detail: Question to Vaibhav, who answers that the SVG is small (719 lines) and the diagram is a transitive reduction of the dependency graph.
cards.landing: Call-graph or architecture tooling (skipped by harness review): output a text form of the boundary graph

cards.source_title: AI That Works #42 No Vibes Allowed
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Vibe coding means you don't give a shit about the code.
cards.claim: He rejects the label 'vibe coding' for spec-driven agent work and calls it software engineering; the reading and thinking is the work.
cards.evidence_detail: Aside while Vaibhav shows lines-of-code charts.
cards.landing: nowhere obvious

cards.source_title: AI That Works #41 Email is All You Need
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: you kind of need to like queue up all the changes you're going to make and then flush
cards.claim: Side effects that cannot be rolled back (sending email, creating calendar events) should be queued as planned writes and only flushed at the end if the run was not interrupted, optionally after a grace period.
cards.evidence_detail: Dex's design answer in a cancellation exercise; Vaibhav adds verify-on-write and send-time re-checks.
cards.landing: Workflow scripts with external effects (publish, comment, PR actions): stage then commit at end
cards.inventory_ref: AI That Works #40 entry (2026-01-19), 'Also #41 Email is All You Need' mention

cards.source_title: AI That Works #41 Email is All You Need
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: you have to like synthetically inject.
cards.claim: If an action happened outside what the model saw (a reply already sent), record it as an event and inject it into the context so the model knows.
cards.evidence_detail: Dex's restatement of Vaibhav's race-condition handling.
cards.landing: Cold-resume: state the agent must be told, written to the repo journal rather than assumed

cards.source_title: AI That Works #41 Email is All You Need
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: deeply putting the engineering back in context engineering
cards.claim: Treating context assembly (what the model is told, which events are injected, thread state) as ordinary systems engineering.
cards.evidence_detail: Reaction to Vaibhav's queue, verify-on-write and thread-reconstruction design.
cards.landing: nowhere obvious

cards.source_title: AI That Works #41 Email is All You Need
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Claude will read the emails and update Markdown files with the status
cards.claim: His working setup forwards email to a webhook that runs a GitHub Actions workflow, where Claude edits a markdown CRM in a private repo, commits and pushes, then posts a Slack summary.
cards.evidence_detail: Running locally via ngrok and deploying to Lambda that day; described as working; no numbers.
cards.landing: Saved workflow/automation pattern: event to Actions to Claude to markdown store to notification; relates to knowledge-store

cards.source_title: AI That Works #41 Email is All You Need
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: The thing that I loved it for was for delegation.
cards.claim: An email-style single inbox suits delegation (forward an item to an agent that files a task, updates a CRM, or researches a person) and helps burn down a backlog without doing each task.
cards.evidence_detail: Personal use; contrasted with Slack as chaotic multi-channel.
cards.landing: nowhere obvious

cards.source_title: AI That Works #40 Applying 12-Factor Principles to Coding Agent SDKs
cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: using agent loops as smaller elements of a deterministic workflow
cards.claim: Squeeze more from coding agents by making each agent loop a small step inside a deterministic workflow stitched with the Claude Agent SDK (microagent workflows).
cards.evidence_detail: Episode description only; no transcript read.
cards.landing: Workflow-tool library of reusable micro-agent scripts

cards.source_title: AI That Works #40 Applying 12-Factor Principles to Coding Agent SDKs
cards.author: Dex+others
cards.quote: session continuation and forking vs. direct compaction
cards.claim: The session covers continuing and forking sessions as an alternative to direct compaction, plus accumulating user rules across context windows and JSON state with Zod.
cards.evidence_detail: Topic list in README/meta only.
cards.landing: Context budget: fork instead of compact; rules accumulation relates to CLAUDE.md growth

cards.source_title: AI That Works #42 No Vibes Allowed
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: you can create a new session and say like, use the iterate design discussion skill
cards.claim: Rather than context-heavy continuation, open a new session and invoke a named skill against the saved design doc to revise it; a fork would preserve the original thread.
cards.evidence_detail: Live use of a skill to update questions four and five; both hosts say better fork UX is wanted.
cards.landing: Skills under .claude/skills/: one skill per stage that edits a named artifact in a fresh session

gaps: The 2026-01-13 episode (12-factor for coding agent SDKs) had no transcript in the bundle; only README and meta were read, so its cards are topic-list level and carry no Dex arguments.

The 2026-01-20 email episode is mostly guest and Vaibhav material (MyMX, queues, threading); only a few Dex remarks were carded. Vaibhav-led ideas (cargo stow boundary enforcement, verify-on-write, S3 thread snapshots) were not carded as Dex's, except where Dex restated or endorsed them.
Transcripts are auto-captions; some quotes contain caption errors (kept verbatim). The 'structured outline' file and prompts shown on screen were not available, so prompt wording is unverified.
Inventory lists #41 and #42 only as a mention inside the #40 entry, not as separate entries, so in_inventory is true with a mention-level reference.
